minutes.headline: Select Board voted to send the FY27 balanced budget and both override tiers to town meeting despite sharp internal debate
minutes.summary: The Select Board finalized its annual town meeting warrant, voting to recommend approval of the FY27 balanced budget, both tiers of the proposed override, and several enterprise fund articles, after lengthy public comment and board debate over cuts to services versus a new assistant town manager position and fourth fire shift. The board also approved the election warrant, appointed a new APDC member, sent a letter opposing state legislation on excise-tax enforcement, and set a budget public information meeting before entering executive session on DPW union negotiations.

what_happened.line: The Select Board voted unanimously to recommend the FY27 balanced budget for town meeting.
The board recommended the override's second tier by a 3-1 vote; the first tier's vote outcome was not audible on the recording.
Public commenters objected to proposed cuts to the library, senior center and beach program alongside new spending on an assistant town manager and a fourth fire shift.
The board also recommended the PAC/PEG, solid waste, water and sewer enterprise fund articles, all unanimously.
The board scheduled a budget public information meeting for the evening of April 28 at the Adult Activity Center.

why_it_matters: Both the balanced budget and the override now go to town meeting, where the choice is between a level-services budget with cuts to programs like the library, senior center and beach program, or an override that funds the assistant town manager position and a fourth fire shift.
A resident weighing the override should note the split board vote on its second tier, which signals the choice was not unanimous even among the officials recommending it.
The April 28 public information meeting is the town's forum for residents to ask about the budget and override before voting.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The two records agree closely on every substantive vote outcome except one: our minutes could not make out the result of the Article M Tier 1 override vote ("not audible"), while the official minutes record it as carried 3-1 with McLeod opposed, and our minutes omit the executive-session entry vote entirely. Most other differences are caption mis-hearings of names and a few cents/dollars, plus a cluster of public-comment figures (Bowen's extra numbers, the $150,000 and $15,000 figures, the excise-tax "$138,000," and a Finance Committee "4-2" vote on the Assistant Town Manager position) that appear only in ours and cannot be checked against the official text as written.
